cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example for the legacy (pre-2010) name: probability of exactly 6 successes in 10 trials at p=0.5
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 0.2050781, the same figure as the modern BINOM.DIST page. Independently derived from the documented mass function: C(10,6)*0.5^10 = 210/1024 = 0.205078125 exactly -> 0.2050781 at 7 dp

cases.description: The same parameters with cumulative TRUE
cases.expected_note: Excel documents the cumulative form as "the probability that there are at most number_s successes". Independently derived: sum over k = 0..6 of C(10,k)*0.5^10 = 848/1024 = 0.828125 exactly
Excel documents: "If number_s < 0 or number_s > trials, BINOMDIST returns the #NUM! error value."
Excel documents: "If probability_s < 0 or probability_s > 1, BINOMDIST returns the #NUM! error value."
Excel documents: "If number_s, trials, or probability_s is nonnumeric, BINOMDIST returns the #VALUE! error value."
